To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measurement of the five key concepts in human-robot interaction (HRI) is important, that we have developed five questionnaires to measure these concepts, and that these questionnaires have been tested for reliability and validity.
We present five questionnaires that can be used to measure the concepts of anthropomorphism, likeability, animacy, perceived intelligence, perceived safety in HRI studies.
the five questionnaires are reliable and valid instruments for measuring the five HRI concepts.

the development of measurement instruments for the anthropomorphism, the perceived intelligence and the likeability of a robot.
the development of a set of questionnaires for the measurement of the five key concepts.
the development and validation of questionnaires that can be used to measure human perceptions of robots.

there are a large number of questionnaires available that measure the five key concepts.
the questionnaires presented in this paper are a good starting point for further research.

we have created a series of questionnaires that can be used to assess five key concepts in the HRI field.
the questionnaires can be considered reliable and valid.
we have developed and validated five questionnaires for five concepts in HRI.

the measurement of these five concepts is possible, but it requires a lot of work to develop reliable and valid questionnaires.
